turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The strongest candidates are those that match the high-performing region of the training set: Pb-based FA/MA mixed-halide absorbers, n-i-p stacks with SnO₂ or TiO₂/SnO₂ electron extraction, Spiro-MeOTAD with Au/Ag contacts, and/or well-designed inverted fullerene/PTAA stacks. I would avoid Bi/Sn-rich, carbon-contact, poorly selective, or unusual no-ETL/no-HTL recipes, since those are consistently lower in the training data.

Top picks:

1. **c079** — FAMAPbBrI with SnO₂-np plus CsPbBr₃-np interfacial/passivation layer, Spiro-MeOTAD/Au. This is very close to the highest-performing SnO₂/FAMAPbBrI family; CsPbBr₃ nanoparticles should passivate interfacial traps and improve extraction.
2. **c062** — FAMAPbBrI on ITO/SnO₂-np | PCBM with Spiro-MeOTAD/MoO₃/Au. SnO₂ + fullerene gives strong electron selectivity and interface passivation, while MoO₃ improves hole-contact energetics.
3. **c092** — FAMAPbI with ITO/SnO₂-np and Spiro-MeOTAD/MoO₃/Ag. Very similar to high-efficiency SnO₂/Spiro devices in the training set; MoO₃ should reduce contact losses.
4. **c038** — CsFAPbI with TiO₂-c | TiO₂-mp | SnO₂-c and Spiro-MeOTAD/Au. The TiO₂/SnO₂ bilayer should improve electron extraction and suppress TiO₂/perovskite recombination; close to high-performing TiO₂/SnO₂ recipes.
5. **c085** — inverted CsFAMAPbBrI with C60 | BCP electron contact and PTAA/PFN-Br/Cu hole contact. This resembles the best p-i-n fullerene/PTAA stacks, with good selectivity and low recombination.

Final: c079, c062, c092, c038, c085
